We have long warned you not to share sensitive personal information in your AI chatbot conversations, as most companies use these conversations as training data – but now there's an even worse problem.

The situation got worse over the weekend, as Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs could be accessed through simple Google searches…

Claude chats leaked

Claude has a share feature that lets you share your chat history with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link that you can send to one or more users, and Claude implicitly assures you that anyone with the link cannot view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered that you don't actually need the link to view the chats. You can simply use Google search, either with specific search terms or by asking Google to show all chat logs shared this way. According to BBC News:

All you actually have to do is tell Google to search the directory used by Claude for shared chats (site:claude.ai/share).

As you'd expect, some of the chats were completely absurd, like someone asking why the music industry is covering up the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But some contained extremely sensitive information, like verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether he needed to proactively disclose a violation; and users accidentally revealing their private keys while seeking help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim that this is not a problem.

The fact is, this is clearly a serious problem, because this is absolutely not what users expected. Worse still, according to Wired, the root cause appears to have been an extremely basic oversight.

This comes just a day after news that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox environment and gain access to all files on a Mac.

How to protect yourself

The issue appears to have been at least partially addressed, as search results that were previously accessible no longer appear, but given that the share feature relies on the flimsy design of 'security through obscurity,' I still recommend avoiding it.

I also recommend deleting all previously shared chats. You can do this under Settings > Privacy > Shared Chats > Manage.

Another vindication of Apple's privacy stance

Apple takes a three-tiered approach to privacy in Apple Intelligence and the new Siri:

  • On-device AI processing whenever possible
  • The first fallback is Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final option is to use a Gemini model with the same level of PCC protections

The sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can ever access or retain any data. The security architecture Apple has designed allows independent verification by security researchers.
